title: Decentralized tenant-aware early-drop and burst-reconciler for Dedicated ingress
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Build a decentralized admission layer for Dedicated fleets that performs tenant-aware early-drop and burst reconciliation at the node level. Goal: preserve per-tenant throughput guarantees (soft floors and hard caps) while reducing tail latency and avoiding global coordination bottlenecks under sudden overloads.
motivation: Current centralized admission strategies create coordination hotspots and add latency during overload; existing shedding features are coarse-grained which causes noisy neighbor impacts. We need a design that enforces guarantees with low coordination overhead and graceful degradation when capacity spikes occur.
design_summary: Introduce a hybrid local-token-reservoir model: each serving node maintains per-tenant local reservoirs (short-lived tokens representing recent throughput entitlement) plus a periodic reconciliation protocol that pulls adjustments from a lightweight global lease service. Admission decisions are made locally using: (1) fast token checks for immediate accepts; (2) probabilistic early-drop when reservoir depleted and predicted short-term demand spike detected; (3) tag-based demotion to best-effort lane with queued reorder. Autoscaler hooks expose headroom metrics per-tenant for reactive scaling.
implementation_notes: Phase 1: implement local reservoirs + early-drop heuristic and a mock global reconciler in the runtime. Phase 2: integrate with fleet lease service for periodic top-ups and downward reconciliation. Phase 3: add autoscaler expose points and rollout policy in Dedicated control plane. Key algorithms: sliding-window token inflation, burst smoothing via EWMA on request arrivals, and epoch-aligned top-up (<= 2s sync). Ensure algorithm works with quantized models and streaming responses.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Under synthetic overload tests, 95th percentile latency degradation for gold tenants <= 30% over baseline and error rate < 0.5% for guaranteed tier. 2) Decreases global coordination RPCs by at least 70% vs centralized admission in scale tests. 3) Autoscaler headroom metric correlated with observed capacity shortfall in long-running soak tests. 4) No customer traffic regression in canary region for 48h.
testing_plan: Unit tests for reservoir logic + deterministic simulator for corner cases. Load tests: ramp-and-spike scenarios with multi-tenant mixes (gold/silver/best-effort). Chaos tests: node restart during reconciliation, network partition between node and lease service. Canary rollout with 5% fleets, metrics dashboard and automatic rollback if customer_impact > medium.
metrics: Per-tenant accept_rate, early_drop_rate, queued_ratio, p50/p95/p99 latency per tenant tier, global coordination_rpc/sec, headroom_estimate, failed_topups. Add dashboard panels and alerts: early_drop_rate > 2% sustained for gold => page on-call.
rollback_plan: Feature gate toggled at node level. If regressions detected revert gate and disable reconciliation in control plane; autoscaler hooks are idempotent and can be toggled off without state loss. Documented rollback playbook and one-click revert in console rollout UI.
updates: 2025-02-12: Spike completed; validated local reservoir approach in single-node simulator. Found token underflow edge case when streaming long-lived connections keep KV cache pinned; added lease decay guard.

2025-02-20: Implemented deterministic early-drop heuristic and added EWMA arrival predictor. Preliminary load tests show 60% reduction in coordination RPCs but early_drop_rate at p95 is ~2.8% for silver tier — tuning ongoing.
2025-02-28: Integrated autoscaler headroom metric export. Added canary hook in control plane; ready for single-region canary deployment.
2025-03-05: Canary 5% rollout started in eu-west-1. Initial telemetry: gold tier p95 latency stable, silver early_drop reduced after reservoir smoothing tweak. No escalations so far.
